111	
112	class AgentWorker:
113	    """Competition agent worker using LiteLLM as the provider layer (ADR-0004)."""
114	
115	    def __init__(
116	        self,
117	        job_id: str,
118	        prompt: str,
119	        policy: JobPolicy,
120	        workspace: Path,
121	        db_url: str | None = None,
122	        model: str | None = None,
123	        dry_run: bool = False,
124	        resume_state: dict | None = None,
125	    ):
126	        self.job_id = job_id
127	        self.prompt = prompt
128	        self.policy = policy
129	        self.workspace = Path(workspace)
130	        self.db_url = db_url
131	        self.dry_run = dry_run
132	        # Optional resume state: {turns_used, cost_usd, last_msg, allow_once}
133	        self.resume_state = resume_state or {}
134	        # model kwarg overrides policy.model when given
135	        if model is not None:
136	            self.policy = JobPolicy(
137	                max_turns=policy.max_turns,
138	                max_cost_usd=policy.max_cost_usd,
139	                max_runtime_s=policy.max_runtime_s,
140	                allowed_tool_patterns=policy.allowed_tool_patterns,
141	                model=model,
142	                temperature=policy.temperature,
143	                top_p=policy.top_p,
144	                min_p=policy.min_p,
145	                approval_gates=policy.approval_gates,
146	                max_side_effect=policy.max_side_effect,
147	                skill_name=getattr(policy, "skill_name", None),
148	                policy_profile=getattr(policy, "policy_profile", "default"),
149	                mode=getattr(policy, "mode", "default"),
150	                tool_decisions=dict(getattr(policy, "tool_decisions", {})),
151	            )
152	        # Allow test code to override the mock scenario or inject a client directly.
153	        self._mock_scenario: str = "two_turns"
154	        self._mock_client: MockLiteLLMClient | None = None
155	
156	    def run(self) -> WorkerResult:
157	        from src.worker import telemetry as _otel
158	
159	        # Only tag spans with a job_id when we know that row exists in the DB
160	        # (otherwise the Supabase exporter trips on the agent_jobs FK).
161	        tracer_job_id = self.job_id if self.db_url else None
162	        tracer = _otel.build_tracer(job_id=tracer_job_id)
163	        if tracer.is_enabled():
164	            job_span = _otel.start_job_span(tracer, self.job_id, self.prompt)
165	            try:
166	                if self.db_url and self.job_id:
167	                    self._safe_set_job_trace(tracer.trace_id, job_span.span_id)
168	            except Exception:
169	                pass
170	        else:
171	            job_span = None
172	        try:
173	            return self._run_inner(tracer)
174	        finally:
175	            if job_span is not None:
176	                job_span.end()
177	
178	    def _safe_set_job_trace(self, trace_id: str, root_span_id: str) -> None:
179	        try:
180	            import sys as _sys
181	
182	            _sys.path.insert(
183	                0, str(Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent.parent / "tools" / "kca")
184	            )
185	            import db as _db
186	
187	            _db.set_job_trace(self.job_id, trace_id, root_span_id)
188	        except Exception:
189	            pass
190	
191	    def _run_inner(self, tracer) -> WorkerResult:
192	        from src.worker import telemetry as _otel
193	
194	        if self._mock_client is not None:
195	            client = self._mock_client
196	        elif self.dry_run:
197	            client = MockLiteLLMClient(scenario=self._mock_scenario)
198	        else:
199	            client = None
200	        budget = BudgetTracker(self.policy, model=self.policy.model)
201	        # Seed from resume_state so cumulative turns/cost roll forward.
202	        if self.resume_state:
203	            budget.turns = int(self.resume_state.get("turns_used") or 0)
204	            budget.cost_usd = float(self.resume_state.get("cost_usd") or 0.0)
205	        executor = ToolExecutor(self.workspace, self.policy)
206	        # One-shot allowlist for the paused tool_input from a prior pause.
207	        allow_once = (self.resume_state or {}).get("allow_once") or None
208	        messages: list[dict] = [{"role": "user", "content": self.prompt}]
209	        start = time.monotonic()
210	
211	        while True:
212	            # 1. Pre-turn budget check
213	            stop_reason = budget.check_limits()
214	            if stop_reason:
215	                self._update_status("failed", error=stop_reason, budget=budget)
216	                return WorkerResult(
217	                    status="budget_stop",
218	                    turns_used=budget.turns,
219	                    cost_usd=budget.cost_usd,
220	                    duration_s=time.monotonic() - start,
221	                    final_message="",
222	                    stop_reason=stop_reason,
223	                )
224	
225	            # 2. LiteLLM call (OpenAI format for all providers)
226	            extra: dict = (
227	                {} if self.policy.min_p is None else {"min_p": self.policy.min_p}
228	            )
229	            with _otel.with_turn_span(tracer, budget.turns + 1) as _turn_span:
230	                if client is not None:
231	                    response = client.completion(
232	                        model=self.policy.model,
233	                        max_tokens=8192,
234	                        tools=TOOL_SCHEMAS,
235	                        messages=messages,
236	                        temperature=self.policy.temperature,
237	                        top_p=self.policy.top_p,
238	                        **extra,
239	                    )
240	                else:
241	                    import litellm
242	
243	                    response = litellm.completion(
244	                        model=self.policy.model,
245	                        max_tokens=8192,
246	                        tools=TOOL_SCHEMAS,
247	                        messages=messages,
248	                        temperature=self.policy.temperature,
249	                        top_p=self.policy.top_p,
250	                        **extra,
251	                    )
252	                if _turn_span is not None:
253	                    _turn_span.set_attribute("model", self.policy.model)
254	                    usage = getattr(response, "usage", None)
255	                    if usage is not None:
256	                        _turn_span.set_attribute(
257	                            "prompt_tokens",
258	                            getattr(usage, "prompt_tokens", 0),
259	                        )
260	                        _turn_span.set_attribute(
261	                            "completion_tokens",
262	                            getattr(usage, "completion_tokens", 0),
263	                        )
264	
265	            # 3. Record turn cost
266	            budget.record_turn(response)
267	            msg = response.choices[0].message
268	            finish_reason = response.choices[0].finish_reason
269	
270	            self._append_event(
271	                "turn_start",
272	                budget.turns,
273	                input_tokens=getattr(response.usage, "prompt_tokens", 0),
274	                output_tokens=getattr(response.usage, "completion_tokens", 0),
275	                cost_usd=budget.cost_usd,
276	                event_data={"finish_reason": finish_reason},
277	            )
278	
279	            # 4. stop → job done
280	            if finish_reason == "stop":
281	                final_text = msg.content or ""
282	                self._update_status("succeeded", budget=budget)
283	                return WorkerResult(
284	                    status="done",
285	                    turns_used=budget.turns,
286	                    cost_usd=budget.cost_usd,
287	                    duration_s=time.monotonic() - start,
288	                    final_message=final_text,
289	                    stop_reason="end_turn",
290	                )
291	
292	            # 5. tool_calls → execute each tool
293	            if finish_reason == "tool_calls":
294	                tool_calls = msg.tool_calls or []
295	                # Append assistant turn with tool_calls (OpenAI message format)
296	                messages.append(
297	                    {
298	                        "role": "assistant",
299	                        "content": msg.content,
300	                        "tool_calls": [
301	                            {
302	                                "id": tc.id,
303	                                "type": "function",
304	                                "function": {
305	                                    "name": tc.function.name,
306	                                    "arguments": tc.function.arguments,
307	                                },
308	                            }
309	                            for tc in tool_calls
310	                        ],
311	                    }
312	                )
313	                for tc in tool_calls:
314	                    tool_input = json.loads(tc.function.arguments)
315	                    self._append_event(
316	                        "tool_call",
317	                        budget.turns,
318	                        event_data={"tool": tc.function.name, "input": tool_input},
319	                    )
320	                    try:
321	                        with _otel.with_tool_span(tracer, tc.function.name, tool_input):
322	                            result_content = self._tool_call(
323	                                executor, tc.function.name, tool_input
324	                            )
325	                    except PolicyViolation as exc:
326	                        # M8 hard-deny path: log + fail the job, no side effects.
327	                        self._update_status(
328	                            "failed",
329	                            error=f"policy_violation: {exc}",
330	                            budget=budget,
331	                        )
332	                        return WorkerResult(
333	                            status="failed",
334	                            turns_used=budget.turns,
335	                            cost_usd=budget.cost_usd,
336	                            duration_s=time.monotonic() - start,
337	                            final_message="",
338	                            stop_reason="policy_violation",
339	                        )
340	                    except ApprovalRequired as exc:
341	                        # One-shot resume allowance: bypass the matching gate
342	                        # exactly once after `kca decisions approve`.
343	                        if allow_once and (
344	                            allow_once.get("operation") == exc.tool_name
345	                            or allow_once.get("operation") == "tool_approval"
346	                        ):
347	                            allow_once = None  # consume
348	                            # Recurse into the actual tool with policy bypass
349	                            # by temporarily relaxing max_side_effect for this
350	                            # one call.
351	                            saved = executor.policy.max_side_effect
352	                            executor.policy.max_side_effect = "SUBMISSION"
353	                            try:
354	                                result_content = executor.execute(
355	                                    tc.function.name, tool_input
356	                                )
357	                            finally:
358	                                executor.policy.max_side_effect = saved
359	                        else:
360	                            return self._handle_approval_required(exc, budget, start)
361	
362	                    self._append_event(
363	                        "tool_result",
364	                        budget.turns,
365	                        event_data={
366	                            "tool": tc.function.name,
367	                            "result_preview": str(result_content)[:200],
368	                        },
369	                    )
370	                    messages.append(
371	                        {
372	                            "role": "tool",
373	                            "tool_call_id": tc.id,
374	                            "content": str(result_content),
375	                        }
376	                    )
377	                continue
378	
379	            # 6. Unexpected finish_reason
380	            self._update_status(
381	                "failed",
382	                error=f"unexpected finish_reason={finish_reason}",
383	                budget=budget,
384	            )
385	            return WorkerResult(
386	                status="failed",
387	                turns_used=budget.turns,
388	                cost_usd=budget.cost_usd,
389	                duration_s=time.monotonic() - start,
390	                final_message="",
391	                stop_reason="unexpected",
392	            )
393	
394	    def _tool_call(
395	        self, executor: "ToolExecutor", tool_name: str, tool_input: dict
396	    ) -> str:
397	        """M8 tool dispatch with ToolSpec + JobPolicy enforcement.
398	
399	        Resolution order:
400	          1. JobPolicy.tool_decisions[tool_name]: "deny" → PolicyViolation;
401	             "ask" → ApprovalRequired (pauses job, records human_decisions);
402	             "allow" or unset → fall through.
403	          2. ToolSpec.sandbox: "unsandboxed" requires the policy decision to
404	             be "allow"; "isolated_workspace" requires cwd to be the job
405	             workspace.
406	          3. ToolSpec.timeout_s wraps the call so a hung tool cannot exceed
407	             the declared budget (applies to ``run_bash`` and other
408	             subprocess-shaped tools; in-process tools observe it via a best
409	             effort signal-based deadline).
410	          4. Every decision is audited via
411	             ``tools.kca.agent.audit.log_policy_decision`` so the
412	             ``agent_tool_audit`` table records the outcome.
413	        """
414	        decision = (self.policy.tool_decisions or {}).get(tool_name)
415	        spec = self._tool_spec(tool_name)
416	        self._audit_tool_decision(
417	            tool_name=tool_name,
418	            decision=decision or "allow",
419	            spec=spec,
420	            tool_input=tool_input,
421	        )
422	
423	        if decision == "deny":
424	            raise PolicyViolation(tool_name, decision="deny")
425	        if decision == "ask":
426	            # Surface as ApprovalRequired so the existing pause/decision flow
427	            # handles it (writes human_decisions + agent_job_events).
428	            side_effect = "LOCAL_WRITE"
429	            if spec is not None:
430	                side_effect = getattr(spec, "side_effect", side_effect) or side_effect
431	            raise ApprovalRequired(tool_name, tool_input, side_effect)
432	
433	        if spec is not None:
434	            self._enforce_tool_spec(spec, tool_input)
435	            timeout = getattr(spec, "timeout_s", None)
436	        else:
437	            timeout = None
438	
439	        if timeout and timeout > 0:
440	            return self._call_with_deadline(executor, tool_name, tool_input, timeout)
441	        return executor.execute(tool_name, tool_input)
442	
443	    def _tool_spec(self, tool_name: str):
444	        """Resolve a ToolSpec from the kca agent tool_registry, if available."""
445	        try:
446	            import sys as _sys
447	
448	            _sys.path.insert(
449	                0,
450	                str(Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent.parent / "tools" / "kca"),
451	            )
452	            from agent.tool_registry import get_tool  # type: ignore
453	
454	            return get_tool(tool_name)
455	        except Exception:
456	            return None
457	
458	    def _enforce_tool_spec(self, spec, tool_input: dict) -> None:
459	        """Cross-check sandbox + isolated_workspace constraints from ToolSpec."""
460	        sandbox = getattr(spec, "sandbox", None)
461	        if sandbox == "isolated_workspace":
462	            # The worker's cwd is the job workspace; tools that resolve paths
463	            # via ToolExecutor._guard_path already reject traversal. We just
464	            # confirm the workspace looks set (a None workspace is a bug).
465	            if not self.workspace:
466	                raise PolicyViolation(spec.name, decision="missing_workspace")
467	        # ``unsandboxed`` requires explicit "allow" — already gated above; this
468	        # is a belt-and-braces check.
469	        if sandbox == "unsandboxed":
470	            decision = (self.policy.tool_decisions or {}).get(spec.name)
471	            if decision != "allow":
472	                raise PolicyViolation(spec.name, decision="unsandboxed_needs_allow")
473	
474	    def _call_with_deadline(
475	        self,
476	        executor: "ToolExecutor",
477	        tool_name: str,
478	        tool_input: dict,
479	        timeout_s: int,
480	    ) -> str:
481	        """Best-effort timeout wrapper. ``run_bash`` already times out via
482	        subprocess; for other tools we just honour the ToolSpec on a wall
483	        clock and surface a string error if exceeded.
484	        """
485	        if tool_name == "run_bash":
486	            ti = dict(tool_input)
487	            ti.setdefault("timeout_s", timeout_s)
488	            return executor.execute(tool_name, ti)
489	        # In-process tools: run inline; if a future tool turns out to be
490	        # blocking we can wrap it with signal.alarm/threading.Timer here.
491	        return executor.execute(tool_name, tool_input)
492	
493	    def _audit_tool_decision(
494	        self,
495	        *,
496	        tool_name: str,
497	        decision: str,
498	        spec,
499	        tool_input: dict,
500	    ) -> None:
501	        try:
502	            import sys as _sys
503	
504	            _sys.path.insert(
505	                0,
506	                str(Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent.parent),
507	            )
508	            from tools.kca.agent.audit import log_policy_decision  # type: ignore
509	
510	            log_policy_decision(
511	                tool=tool_name,
512	                operation=tool_name,
513	                decision=decision,
514	                skill_name=self.policy.skill_name,
515	                mode=self.policy.mode,
516	                policy_profile=self.policy.policy_profile,
517	                args=tool_input,
518	                audit_required=bool(getattr(spec, "audit_required", False))
519	                if spec is not None
520	                else False,
521	                job_id=self.job_id if self.db_url else None,
522	            )
523	        except Exception as exc:  # pragma: no cover
524	            import sys as _sys
525	
526	            _sys.stderr.write(f"[audit warn] {exc}\n")
527	
528	    def _handle_approval_required(
529	        self, exc: ApprovalRequired, budget: BudgetTracker, start: float
530	    ) -> WorkerResult:
531	        """Pause the job and record a decision request.
532	
533	        M6: when the gating operation is one of KCA_REVIEWER_TRIGGER_OPS,
534	        first consult the sync reviewer. Reviewer.approve auto-resumes,
535	        reviewer.reject either escalates to humans (default) or fails the
536	        job (when KCA_REVIEWER_ESCALATE_REJECT=0), and reviewer.abstain
537	        falls through to the existing human-decisions path.
538	        """
539	        # ------------------------------------------------------------------
540	        # M6 reviewer pre-check
541	        # ------------------------------------------------------------------
542	        reviewer_outcome = self._maybe_consult_reviewer(exc, budget)
543	        if reviewer_outcome == "approve":
544	            # Re-execute the gated tool with one-shot bypass.
545	            return WorkerResult(
546	                status="reviewer_approved",
547	                turns_used=budget.turns,
548	                cost_usd=budget.cost_usd,
549	                duration_s=time.monotonic() - start,
550	                final_message="reviewer approved",
551	                stop_reason="reviewer_approve",
552	            )
553	        if reviewer_outcome == "reject_fail":
554	            self._update_status(
555	                "failed",
556	                error="reviewer rejected high-stakes operation",
557	                budget=budget,
558	            )
559	            return WorkerResult(
560	                status="failed",
561	                turns_used=budget.turns,
562	                cost_usd=budget.cost_usd,
563	                duration_s=time.monotonic() - start,
564	                final_message="",
565	                stop_reason="reviewer_reject",
566	            )
567	        # reviewer_outcome in {None, "reject_escalate", "abstain"} — fall
568	        # through to human-decisions flow.
569	        decision_id = None
570	        if self.db_url:
571	            try:
572	                import sys
573	
574	                sys.path.insert(
575	                    0,
576	                    str(
577	                        Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent.parent / "tools" / "kca"
578	                    ),
579	                )
580	                import db as _db
581	
582	                decision_id = _db.insert_approval_request(
583	                    decision_type="tool_approval",
584	                    prompt=f"Worker job {self.job_id} wants to call {exc.tool_name}",
585	                    options={
586	                        "approve": "allow this tool call",
587	                        "deny": "block and stop job",
588	                    },
589	                    job_id=self.job_id,
590	                )
591	                _db.update_job(
592	                    self.job_id,
593	                    status="paused",
594	                    turns_used=budget.turns,
595	                    cost_usd=budget.cost_usd,
596	                )
597	            except Exception:
598	                pass
599	        self._append_event(
600	            "approval_pause",
601	            budget.turns,
602	            event_data={
603	                "tool": exc.tool_name,
604	                "operation": exc.tool_name,
605	                "tool_input": exc.tool_input,
606	                "side_effect": exc.side_effect,
607	                "decision_id": decision_id,
608	            },
609	        )
610	        import sys
611	
612	        print(
613	            f"JOB PAUSED — run `kca decisions approve --id {decision_id}` to resume",
614	            file=sys.stderr,
615	        )
616	        return WorkerResult(
617	            status="paused",
618	            turns_used=budget.turns,
619	            cost_usd=budget.cost_usd,
620	            duration_s=time.monotonic() - start,
621	            final_message=f"Waiting for approval: decision_id={decision_id}",
622	            stop_reason="approval_required",
623	        )
624	
625	    @classmethod
626	    def resume(
627	        cls,
628	        job_id: str,
629	        *,
630	        workspace: Path,
631	        policy: JobPolicy | None = None,
632	        db_url: str | None = None,
633	        dry_run: bool = False,
634	    ) -> "AgentWorker":
635	        """Construct an AgentWorker primed from prior agent_job_events.
636	
637	        Reads the job row + events; reconstructs (turns_used, cost_usd) and
638	        seeds a one-shot approval allowlist for the paused tool_input so the
639	        next gate check passes once.
640	        """
641	        import sys as _sys
642	
643	        _sys.path.insert(
644	            0, str(Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent.parent / "tools" / "kca")
645	        )
646	        import db as _db
647	
648	        job = _db.get_job(job_id)
649	        events = _db.list_job_events(job_id)
650	        turns = int(job.get("turns_used") or 0)
651	        cost = float(job.get("cost_usd") or 0)
652	        last_pause_input = None
653	        last_pause_op = None
654	        # Walk events: the most recent approval_pause defines the next-resume
655	        # allowlist entry, unless followed by an approval_resume already
656	        # consumed in a previous resume attempt.
657	        for ev in events:
658	            t = ev.get("event_type")
659	            ed = ev.get("event_data") or {}
660	            if isinstance(ed, str):
661	                try:
662	                    ed = json.loads(ed)
663	                except Exception:
664	                    ed = {}
665	            if t == "approval_pause":
666	                last_pause_input = ed.get("tool_input")
667	                last_pause_op = ed.get("operation") or ed.get("tool")
668	            elif t == "approval_resume":
669	                # Resume consumed; clear pending allowance.
670	                last_pause_input = None
671	                last_pause_op = None
672	        prompt = job.get("prompt") or ""
673	        policy = policy or JobPolicy()
674	        worker = cls(
675	            job_id=job_id,
676	            prompt=prompt,
677	            policy=policy,
678	            workspace=workspace,
679	            db_url=db_url,
680	            dry_run=dry_run,
681	            resume_state={
682	                "turns_used": turns,
683	                "cost_usd": cost,
684	                "allow_once": {
685	                    "operation": last_pause_op,
686	                    "tool_input": last_pause_input,
687	                }
688	                if last_pause_op
689	                else None,
690	            },
691	        )
692	        return worker
693	
694	    def _maybe_consult_reviewer(
695	        self, exc: ApprovalRequired, budget: BudgetTracker
696	    ) -> str | None:
697	        """Run the sync reviewer for trigger ops; return outcome tag.
698	
699	        Returns one of:
700	          None             — reviewer not consulted (op not in trigger set or
701	                              already reviewed)
702	          "approve"        — reviewer approved; caller resumes the tool
703	          "reject_fail"    — reviewer rejected and ESCALATE_REJECT=0
704	          "reject_escalate"— reviewer rejected, caller should page humans
705	          "abstain"        — reviewer abstained, caller should page humans
706	        """
707	        from src.worker.reviewer import (
708	            Reviewer,
709	            ReviewRequest,
710	            should_consult_reviewer,
711	            escalate_reject,
712	        )
713	
714	        target_op = exc.tool_name
715	        if not should_consult_reviewer(target_op):
716	            return None
717	        if not self.db_url:
718	            # No DB → no event trail and no place to record the verdict.
719	            # The dry-run worker still records the reviewer span via OTEL when
720	            # T005 wires it up; for now just skip silently.
721	            return None
722	        try:
723	            import sys as _sys
724	
725	            _sys.path.insert(
726	                0, str(Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent.parent / "tools" / "kca")
727	            )
728	            import db as _db
729	
730	            # Skip if reviewer already ran for (job_id, target_op).
731	            try:
732	                existing = _db.find_review_for_op(self.job_id, target_op)
733	            except Exception:
734	                existing = None
735	            if existing is not None:
736	                return None
737	            events = []
738	            try:
739	                events = _db.list_job_events(self.job_id)
740	            except Exception:
741	                events = []
742	            req = ReviewRequest(
743	                job_id=self.job_id,
744	                target_op=target_op,
745	                tool_name=exc.tool_name,
746	                tool_input=exc.tool_input,
747	                final_message=None,
748	                event_trail=events,
749	            )
750	            reviewer = Reviewer(dry_run=self.dry_run)
751	            verdict = reviewer.review(req)
752	            try:
753	                _db.create_review(
754	                    job_id=self.job_id,
755	                    reviewer_model=verdict.reviewer_model,
756	                    verdict=verdict.verdict,
757	                    target_op=target_op,
758	                    rationale=verdict.rationale,
759	                    evidence=verdict.evidence,
760	                    cost_usd=verdict.cost_usd,
761	                )
762	            except Exception:
763	                pass
764	            if verdict.verdict == "approve":
765	                self._append_event(
766	                    "approval_resume",
767	                    budget.turns,
768	                    event_data={
769	                        "source": "reviewer",
770	                        "verdict": "approve",
771	                        "target_op": target_op,
772	                        "rationale": verdict.rationale[:200],
773	                    },
774	                )
775	                return "approve"
776	            if verdict.verdict == "reject":
777	                if escalate_reject():
778	                    self._append_event(
779	                        "reviewer_reject",
780	                        budget.turns,
781	                        event_data={
782	                            "target_op": target_op,
783	                            "rationale": verdict.rationale[:200],
784	                            "escalated": True,
785	                        },
786	                    )
787	                    return "reject_escalate"
788	                self._append_event(
789	                    "reviewer_reject",
790	                    budget.turns,
791	                    event_data={
792	                        "target_op": target_op,
793	                        "rationale": verdict.rationale[:200],
794	                        "escalated": False,
795	                    },
796	                )
797	                return "reject_fail"
798	            # abstain → fall through
799	            self._append_event(
800	                "reviewer_abstain",
801	                budget.turns,
802	                event_data={
803	                    "target_op": target_op,
804	                    "rationale": verdict.rationale[:200],
805	                },
806	            )
807	            return "abstain"
808	        except Exception:
809	            return None
810	
811	    def _append_event(
812	        self,
813	        event_type: str,
814	        turn_number: int,
815	        *,
816	        input_tokens: int | None = None,
817	        output_tokens: int | None = None,
818	        cost_usd: float | None = None,
819	        event_data: dict | None = None,
820	    ) -> None:
821	        if not self.db_url:
822	            return
823	        try:
824	            import sys
825	
826	            sys.path.insert(
827	                0, str(Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent.parent / "tools" / "kca")
828	            )
829	            import db as _db
830	
831	            _db.append_job_event(
832	                self.job_id,
833	                event_type,
834	                turn_number=turn_number,
835	                input_tokens=input_tokens,
836	                output_tokens=output_tokens,
837	                cost_usd=cost_usd,
838	                event_data=event_data or {},
839	            )
840	        except Exception:
841	            pass

633	def _lease_job(
634	    conn: "psycopg.Connection",

644	                   leased_by = %s,
645	                   leased_until = now() + (%s || ' seconds')::interval,
646	                   started_at = COALESCE(started_at, now())

117	    """Return True if side-effect a >= b in severity."""

142	    cmd = command.strip()

146	    for pat in _HARD_DENY_PATTERNS:

149	    for pat in policy.allowed_tool_patterns:

<details>
<summary><code>/home/harry/test/tt_pangu/scripts/m9_t003_drive_reviewer_gate.py</code></summary>

```python
"""M9-T003: drive the worker to fire the reviewer-gate on kaggle_submit.

This script:
  1. Creates a real agent_jobs row tied to the Spaceship Titanic baseline run.
  2. Runs AgentWorker with a MockLiteLLMClient that emits one synthetic
     `kaggle_submit` tool call (tool_decisions["kaggle_submit"]="ask"
     forces ApprovalRequired into _handle_approval_required).
  3. Forces the sync reviewer to ABSTAIN (no live LLM call) so the
     handler writes an agent_reviews row (verdict='abstain') AND falls
     through to the human-decisions branch — inserting a pending
     human_decisions row tied to the job.
  4. Prints job_id / review_id / decision_id for the closeout report.

The script never invokes `kaggle competitions submit`. The worker stops
with `stop_reason="approval_required"` after pausing the job.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import json
import os
import sys
import types
from pathlib import Path

REPO_ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent
sys.path.insert(0, str(REPO_ROOT))
sys.path.insert(0, str(REPO_ROOT / "tools" / "kca"))

import db as _db  # type: ignore  # noqa: E402

from src.worker._types import JobPolicy  # noqa: E402
from src.worker.worker import AgentWorker, MockLiteLLMClient  # noqa: E402
from src.worker import reviewer as reviewer_mod  # noqa: E402


def _single_kaggle_submit_client() -> MockLiteLLMClient:
    """LiteLLM mock: emit one `kaggle_submit` tool call, then stop."""

    client = MockLiteLLMClient(scenario="two_turns")
    turn = {"n": 0}

    def completion(**_kwargs):
        turn["n"] += 1
        if turn["n"] == 1:
            tc = types.SimpleNamespace(
                id="call_submit_0",
                type="function",
                function=types.SimpleNamespace(
                    name="kaggle_submit",
                    arguments=json.dumps(
                        {
                            "competition": "spaceship-titanic",
                            "file": "runs/spaceship-titanic/baseline-lr/submission.csv",
                            "message": "M9-T002 baseline LR (M9-T003 reviewer gate)",
                        }
                    ),
                ),
            )
            msg = types.SimpleNamespace(content=None, tool_calls=[tc])
            choice = types.SimpleNamespace(message=msg, finish_reason="tool_calls")
            return types.SimpleNamespace(
                choices=[choice],
                usage=types.SimpleNamespace(prompt_tokens=20, completion_tokens=10),
            )
        msg = types.SimpleNamespace(content="done", tool_calls=None)
        choice = types.SimpleNamespace(message=msg, finish_reason="stop")
        return types.SimpleNamespace(
            choices=[choice],
            usage=types.SimpleNamespace(prompt_tokens=10, completion_tokens=5),
        )

    client.completion = completion  # type: ignore[method-assign]
    return client


class _AbstainReviewer:
    """Sync reviewer stub that always abstains. Never calls a real LLM."""

    def __init__(self, *_args, **_kwargs):
        self.model = "stub-abstain"
        self.dry_run = False

    def review(self, _req):
        return reviewer_mod.ReviewVerdict(
            verdict="abstain",
            rationale="M9-T003 driver: forced abstain to exercise human-decisions path",
            evidence={"mode": "m9_t003_stub"},
            cost_usd=0.0,
            reviewer_model=self.model,
        )


def main() -> int:
    db_url = os.environ.get("SUPABASE_DB_URL")
    if not db_url:
        print("SUPABASE_DB_URL not set", file=sys.stderr)
        return 2

    # Patch reviewer to abstain, so the handler records agent_reviews AND
    # falls through to insert_approval_request (human_decisions pending).
    reviewer_mod.Reviewer = _AbstainReviewer  # type: ignore[assignment]

    # Build a real agent_jobs row tied to the spaceship-titanic competition.
    policy_payload = {
        "max_turns": 4,
        "model": "claude-sonnet-4-6",
        "tool_decisions": {"kaggle_submit": "ask"},
    }
    job_id = _db.create_job(
        project_id=_db.DEFAULT_PROJECT_ID,
        prompt="M9-T003 driver: submit spaceship-titanic baseline",
        policy=policy_payload,
        model="claude-sonnet-4-6",
        competition_slug="spaceship-titanic",
    )
    print(f"job_id={job_id}")

    policy = JobPolicy(
        max_turns=4,
        skill_name="m9-t003-driver",
        policy_profile="default",
        mode="default",
        tool_decisions={"kaggle_submit": "ask"},
    )
    workspace = REPO_ROOT
    worker = AgentWorker(
        job_id=job_id,
        prompt="M9-T003 driver: submit spaceship-titanic baseline",
        policy=policy,
        workspace=workspace,
        db_url=db_url,
        dry_run=True,  # avoid real LiteLLM in the worker main loop
    )
    worker._mock_client = _single_kaggle_submit_client()
    result = worker.run()
    print(f"worker.status={result.status} stop_reason={result.stop_reason}")

    # Surface the agent_reviews + human_decisions rows for closeout.
    review = _db.find_review_for_op(job_id, "kaggle_submit")
    print(f"agent_reviews.id={review['id'] if review else None} verdict={review['verdict'] if review else None}")

    pending = _db.list_pending_decisions(job_id=job_id)
    print(f"human_decisions pending count={len(pending)}")
    if pending:
        print(f"human_decisions.id={pending[0]['id']} status={pending[0]['status']}")

    # List job events so the closeout can cite the approval_pause event.
    events = _db.list_job_events(job_id)
    types_only = [(e.get("event_type"), (e.get("event_data") or {}).get("operation") or (e.get("event_data") or {}).get("target_op") or "") for e in events]
    print(f"events={types_only}")

    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    raise SystemExit(main())

```

1	# Milestone Loop Protocol
2	
3	_Shared rules that apply to every milestone Loop Prompt (M0+) unless a
4	milestone explicitly overrides one._
5	
6	Each `docs/m*-loop-prompts.md` should reference this file once at the top
7	rather than duplicating the rules per prompt.
8	
9	---
10	
11	## 1. Sequencing
12	
13	- Loop Prompts within a milestone MUST execute in order.
14	- Each prompt's **acceptance checks MUST pass** before moving to the next.
15	- On failure: fix the specific issue and **retry that prompt only**; do
16	  not skip ahead and do not redo prompts that already passed.
17	
18	## 2. External systems and side effects
19	
20	- Do NOT call the **real Anthropic API or Kaggle API** outside of paths
21	  the milestone explicitly designates as live; default to `--dry-run`.
22	- Do NOT run real **Kaggle submit / kernel push / dataset upload /
23	  model upload** unless the milestone explicitly requests it AND a
24	  human-approval record exists.
25	- Do NOT change **production Supabase**.
26	
27	## 3. Database validation
28	
29	- Use `SUPABASE_DB_URL=postgresql://postgres:s3cr3t@172.21.0.4:5432/postgres`
30	  — the `supabase-db` container on the local Docker network.
31	- Container IPs change on `docker compose down/up`; refresh with:
32	  ```bash
33	  docker inspect supabase-db \
34	    --format '{{range .NetworkSettings.Networks}}{{.IPAddress}}{{end}}'
35	  ```
36	- DB calls and LAN-host calls require `dangerouslyDisableSandbox=true`.
37	  Cloud LLM calls stay **inside** the sandbox.
38	
39	## 4. Reporting
40	
41	- Report **PASS / FAIL / SKIP** inline for each prompt's verification
42	  step.
43	- At milestone end, write the milestone's defined **Closeout format**
44	  (see each milestone's last Loop Prompt for the exact fields).
45	
46	## 5. Git / GitHub — worktree mode
47	
48	This project executes each milestone inside a dedicated **git worktree**
49	branched off `main`.
50	
51	- **Mid-milestone, mid-prompt:** do not `git commit` or `git push`
52	  unless the individual task spec explicitly says so. Stage with
53	  `git add` and surface diffs in the inline report.
54	- **At milestone end** — once every Loop Prompt has PASSed and the
55	  milestone's Closeout has been written — Claude Code SHOULD:
56	  1. `git add` only the files listed in the Closeout's "files changed"
57	     section (or its equivalent).
58	  2. `git commit` using either:
59	     - one squash commit per milestone, OR
60	     - one commit per Loop Prompt,
61	     depending on the milestone's preference. The default is **one
62	     commit per Loop Prompt**, with the milestone's final review as the
63	     last commit.
64	  3. `git push` the worktree's branch to the remote.
65	  4. `gh pr create` against `main` using the milestone's
66	     `docs/m{N}-final-review.md` as the PR body.
67	
68	- The following **still require explicit human approval** at any time:
69	  - `git push --force` (any branch)
70	  - `gh pr merge` (any PR)
71	  - any push to `main` directly
72	  - any `gh label create/edit/delete`, `gh issue edit/comment`,
73	    `gh pr edit/comment` against issues or PRs **not** owned by this
74	    milestone
75	
76	- If the milestone's task spec or scope says
77	  "do not commit / push / open PRs", that override **wins** — typically
78	  used for planning-only or evidence-only milestones.
79	
80	## 6. Secrets and forbidden reads
81	
82	These are always denied, regardless of milestone:
83	
84	- `.env*`
85	- `**/kaggle.json`, `~/.kaggle/kaggle.json`
86	- `~/.ssh/id_rsa`, `~/.ssh/id_ed25519`, any private key contents
87	- `~/.aws/**`, `~/.config/gcloud/**`
88	- `secrets/**`
89	
90	Shell commands that would surface the above (`cat`, `grep`, `head`,
91	`tail`, `less`, `more`, file uploads) over these paths are blocked at
92	the hook layer.
93	
94	---
95	
96	## How a milestone references this file
97	
98	In each Loop Prompt block, instead of repeating the rules above, include
99	one line near the top:
100	
101	```
102	Follow: docs/milestone-loop-protocol.md
103	```
104	
105	A milestone's `docs/m{N}-loop-prompts.md` should still spell out:
106	
107	- the milestone's own scope, non-goals, and task list;
108	- per-Loop-Prompt read lists, scope, acceptance criteria;
109	- any **override** of a default in this file (e.g. a planning-only
110	  milestone overriding the worktree commit/push behavior).
111	
````

319	## GitHub issue / label workflow for M9
320	
321	Each M9 task is filed as a GitHub issue using the `feature-work.yml` form,
322	labelled per task type:
323	
324	| Task | Issue labels at file time | Labels added by triage | Labels at merge |
325	|---|---|---|---|
326	| M9-T000 | `type:feature`, `ai:triage`, `area:kaggle`, `area:config`, `area:security` | `ai:ready` (after AC + owner) | `ai:implementing` → close |
327	| M9-T001 | `type:feature`, `ai:triage`, `area:kaggle` | `ai:ready` | `ai:implementing` → close |
328	| M9-T002 | `type:feature`, `ai:triage`, `area:worker`, `area:kaggle` | `ai:ready` | `ai:implementing` → close |
329	| M9-T003 | `type:feature`, `ai:triage`, `area:worker`, `area:supabase`, `area:ui` | `ai:ready` | `ai:implementing` → close |
330	| M9-T004 | `type:feature`, `ai:blocked`, `policy:approval-required`, `decision:needed`, `area:kaggle`, `priority:P0` | `decision:confirmed` + `ai:ready` only after human comment "approved to submit" | `ai:implementing` → close |
331	| M9-T005 | `type:feature`, `ai:triage`, `area:worker`, `area:kaggle` | `ai:ready` | `ai:implementing` → close |
332	| M9-T006 | `type:test-gap`, `ai:triage`, `area:testing` | `ai:ready` | `ai:implementing` → close |
333	| M9-T007 | `type:test-gap`, `ai:triage`, `area:testing`, `area:ci` | `ai:ready` | `ai:implementing` → close |
334	| M9-T008 | `type:feature`, `ai:triage`, `area:release`, `area:docs` | `ai:ready` after T000–T007 closed | `ai:implementing` → close |
335	
336	T004 is the only task that starts `ai:blocked` and requires a
337	`decision:confirmed` comment with an explicit "approved to submit" record
338	before triage may promote it to `ai:ready`. This is enforced by the
339	`github-issue-triage` agent rules in `.claude/skills/github-issue-triage/`.
340	
341	The PR for each task uses `.github/pull_request_template.md`. The
342	"Remote side effects" section is load-bearing: T004's PR is the ONLY
343	M9 PR that may check the "Live Kaggle call" box, and must link the
344	approval comment from the closing issue.

347	
348	## Approval gates (summary)
349	
350	| Gate | When it fires | Where the approval is recorded | Who can approve |
351	|---|---|---|---|
352	| `kaggle_submit` | Worker stages a submission file and calls into `tools/kca/kg.py::cmd_submit` | `human_decisions` row + comment on the closing GitHub issue | Project owner / reviewer named on the issue |
353	| `kernel_push` | Not used in M9 | n/a (out of scope) | n/a |
354	| `dataset_upload` | Not used in M9 | n/a (out of scope) | n/a |
355	| `model_upload` | Not used in M9 | n/a (out of scope) | n/a |
356	
357	The Kaggle approval flow inside M9 is:
358	
359	```
360	worker stages submission.csv
361	  → reviewer-gate writes agent_reviews row + agent_job_events
362	  → decision_api surfaces pending decision (POST /decisions queued)
363	  → UI Approval Inbox renders pending decision
364	  → human approves via UI (POST /decisions/<id>/approve) OR
365	    `kca decisions approve --id <id>`
366	  → human comments "approved to submit" on the closing issue
367	  → triage agent promotes issue to `decision:confirmed` + `ai:ready`
368	  → M9-T004 Loop Prompt runs ONE `kca kaggle submit`
369	  → LB score recorded; submissions row written
370	  → PR opens with the approval comment linked
371	```
372	
373	A second real Kaggle submission inside M9 is **out of scope**. If a
374	follow-up experiment in M9-T005 turns out to need its own LB score,
375	file it as a new M10+ issue and gate it the same way.
376

397	## Rollback / stop criteria
398	
399	Stop the milestone — do **not** advance to the next Loop Prompt — if any of
400	these is true:
401	
402	- A real Kaggle submit returns an error from Kaggle (rate limit, bad CSV,
403	  rules violation). The fix path is local: regenerate the submission and
404	  re-request approval; do NOT silently retry.
405	- The reviewer gate (M9-T003) fails to fire when it should, or fires
406	  when it shouldn't.
407	- Any `policy:approval-required` issue advances without the corresponding
408	  `decision:confirmed` label and comment.
409	- Any test in the validation suite regresses from green to red.
410	- The DSN, credentials, or `.env*` are accidentally printed in any log,
411	  audit row, or PR. Stop and rotate the credential immediately.
412	- CV scores diverge from the M9-T006 thresholds in a way that suggests a
413	  leakage bug (e.g. CV near 1.0). Investigate before submitting.
414	
415	If M9 needs a new architectural decision (e.g. multi-user auth, a new
416	queue, or a new artifact storage shape), **pause and ask** — those are
417	M10+ decisions, not M9 expansion. Open an ADR draft in `docs/adr/` and
418	stop the milestone there.

33	class ApprovalRequired(Exception):
34	    """Raised when a gated operation lacks approval under the active policy."""
35	
36	    def __init__(self, operation: str, policy: dict):
37	        self.operation = operation
38	        self.policy = policy
39	        super().__init__(f"ApprovalRequired: {operation}")

41	
42	def _check_approval_gate(operation: str, policy: dict) -> None:
43	    """Raise ApprovalRequired if `policy` (or defaults) gates `operation`.
44	
45	    KCA_ALLOW_REMOTE=1 remains an emergency CI override.
46	    """
47	    gates = (policy or {}).get("approval_gates", {})
48	    requires = gates.get(operation, OPERATION_DEFAULTS.get(operation, True))
49	    if requires and not os.environ.get(_GATE_ENV):
50	        raise ApprovalRequired(operation, policy or {})
51	
52	
53	def _gate(side_effect: SideEffect, command_name: str) -> tuple[bool, str | None]:
54	    if side_effect in (SideEffect.READ_ONLY, SideEffect.LOCAL_WRITE):
55	        return True, None
56	    if os.environ.get(_GATE_ENV) == "1":
57	        warn(f"REMOTE OPERATION: kaggle {command_name} — {_GATE_ENV} is set")
58	        return True, None
59	    return False, f"remote operation requires {_GATE_ENV}=1 and human approval"
60	
61	
62	def _record_approval(command_name: str, options: dict) -> tuple[str | None, str | None]:
63	    """Insert a pending human_decisions row. Returns (approval_id, warning).
64	
65	    Best-effort: DB failures never block the refusal path. Caller emits the
66	    blocked envelope regardless.
67	    """
68	    args_summary = ", ".join(f"{k}={v}" for k, v in options.items() if v is not None)
69	    prompt = f"Approve Kaggle {command_name} ({args_summary or 'no args'})"
70	    try:
71	        approval_id = db.insert_approval_request(
72	            decision_type=f"kaggle.{command_name}",
73	            prompt=prompt,
74	            options=options,
75	        )
76	        return approval_id, None
77	    except Exception as e:
78	        return None, f"approval recording failed: {type(e).__name__}: {e}"

83	    side_effect: SideEffect,
84	    reason: str,
85	    options: dict | None = None,
86	) -> int:

277	def _sha256_file(p: Path) -> str:
278	    h = hashlib.sha256()
279	    with p.open("rb") as f:
280	        for chunk in iter(lambda: f.read(1 << 20), b""):
281	            h.update(chunk)
282	    return h.hexdigest()
283	
284	
285	def _walk_files(root: Path) -> list[Path]:
286	    out: list[Path] = []
287	    for child in sorted(root.rglob("*")):
288	        if child.is_file() and child.name != "manifest.json":
289	            out.append(child)
290	    return out
291	
292	
293	def cmd_download(args: argparse.Namespace) -> int:
294	    se = SideEffect.LOCAL_WRITE
295	    competition = args.competition
296	    path_str = args.path or str(Path.cwd() / "data" / competition)
297	    path = Path(path_str)
298	    path.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
299	    manifest_path = path / "manifest.json"
300	
301	    existing: dict = {"files": []}
302	    if manifest_path.exists():
303	        try:
304	            existing = json.loads(manifest_path.read_text())
305	        except json.JSONDecodeError:
306	            existing = {"files": []}
307	
308	    skipped = 0
309	    if args.resume and existing.get("files"):
310	        # Walk existing manifest; if file on disk matches sha256, skip its
311	        # re-download by removing it from a "to download" list. Since the
312	        # kaggle CLI fetches the whole bundle, we cannot truly skip per-file
313	        # — but we record how many files matched so the caller knows the
314	        # resume comparison ran. The actual download is still invoked unless
315	        # every file matched.
316	        all_matched = True
317	        for entry in existing.get("files", []):
318	            target = path / entry["name"]
319	            if target.exists() and _sha256_file(target) == entry.get("sha256"):
320	                skipped += 1
321	            else:
322	                all_matched = False
323	        if all_matched and skipped > 0:
324	            # Nothing left to fetch; just refresh manifest and return.
325	            return _refresh_manifest_and_emit(
326	                competition=competition,
327	                path=path,
328	                manifest_path=manifest_path,
329	                skipped=skipped,
330	                rc=0,
331	                stdout="",
332	                stderr="",
333	                ran_kaggle=False,
334	                side_effect=se,
335	            )
336	
337	    # Run kaggle CLI; if it isn't installed or creds missing, surface a
338	    # graceful error and still build/refresh the manifest from whatever is
339	    # already on disk (useful for tests and --resume scenarios).
340	    rc = 0
341	    stdout = ""
342	    stderr = ""
343	    try:
344	        proc = subprocess.run(
345	            ["kaggle", "competitions", "download", "-c", competition, "-p", str(path)],
346	            capture_output=True,
347	            text=True,
348	        )
349	        rc = proc.returncode
350	        stdout = proc.stdout or ""
351	        stderr = proc.stderr or ""
352	    except FileNotFoundError as e:
353	        rc = 127
354	        stderr = f"kaggle CLI not found: {e}"
355	
356	    return _refresh_manifest_and_emit(
357	        competition=competition,
358	        path=path,
359	        manifest_path=manifest_path,
360	        skipped=skipped,
361	        rc=rc,
362	        stdout=stdout,
363	        stderr=stderr,
364	        ran_kaggle=True,
365	        side_effect=se,
366	    )
367	
368	
369	def _refresh_manifest_and_emit(
370	    *,
371	    competition: str,
372	    path: Path,
373	    manifest_path: Path,
374	    skipped: int,
375	    rc: int,
376	    stdout: str,
377	    stderr: str,
378	    ran_kaggle: bool,
379	    side_effect: SideEffect,
380	) -> int:
381	    files = _walk_files(path)
382	    entries = []
383	    for f in files:
384	        rel = f.relative_to(path).as_posix()
385	        entries.append(
386	            {
387	                "name": rel,
388	                "sha256": _sha256_file(f),
389	                "bytes": f.stat().st_size,
390	            }
391	        )
392	    manifest = {
393	        "competition": competition,
394	        "fetched_at": _dt.datetime.utcnow().isoformat() + "Z",
395	        "files": entries,
396	    }
397	    manifest_path.write_text(json.dumps(manifest, indent=2))
398	    payload = {
399	        "ok": rc == 0,
400	        "competition": competition,
401	        "path": str(path),
402	        "files": len(entries),
403	        "skipped": skipped,
404	        "manifest": str(manifest_path),
405	        "side_effect": side_effect.value,
406	    }
407	    if not ran_kaggle:
408	        payload["all_matched"] = True
409	    if stdout:
410	        payload["stdout"] = stdout
411	    if stderr:
412	        payload["stderr"] = stderr
413	    return _emit_json(payload)
414

416	def cmd_verify(args: argparse.Namespace) -> int:
417	    se = SideEffect.READ_ONLY
418	    path = Path(args.path)
419	    manifest_path = path / "manifest.json"
420	    if not manifest_path.exists():
421	        return _emit_json(
422	            {
423	                "ok": False,
424	                "error": f"manifest not found: {manifest_path}",
425	                "path": str(path),
426	                "side_effect": se.value,
427	            }
428	        )
429	    try:
430	        manifest = json.loads(manifest_path.read_text())
431	    except json.JSONDecodeError as e:
432	        return _emit_json(
433	            {
434	                "ok": False,
435	                "error": f"manifest parse error: {e}",
436	                "path": str(path),
437	                "side_effect": se.value,
438	            }
439	        )
440	    ok_count = 0
441	    missing: list[str] = []
442	    mismatched: list[str] = []
443	    for entry in manifest.get("files", []):
444	        name = entry["name"]
445	        target = path / name
446	        if not target.exists():
447	            missing.append(name)
448	            continue
449	        if _sha256_file(target) != entry.get("sha256"):
450	            mismatched.append(name)
451	            continue
452	        ok_count += 1
453	    return _emit_json(
454	        {
455	            "ok": (not missing) and (not mismatched),
456	            "ok_count": ok_count,
457	            "missing": missing,
458	            "mismatched": mismatched,
459	            "path": str(path),
460	            "side_effect": se.value,
461	        }
462	    )
463

465	def cmd_watch(args: argparse.Namespace) -> int:
466	    kernel_ref = getattr(args, "kernel", None) or args.run
467	    poll_seconds = getattr(args, "poll_seconds", 30)
468	    max_iterations = getattr(args, "max_iterations", 1)
469	    final_status = "unknown"
470	    last_stdout = ""
471	    for _ in range(max_iterations):
472	        proc = subprocess.run(
473	            ["kaggle", "kernels", "status", kernel_ref],
474	            capture_output=True,
475	            text=True,
476	        )
477	        last_stdout = proc.stdout
478	        text = (proc.stdout or "").lower()
479	        if "complete" in text:
480	            final_status = "complete"
481	            break
482	        if "error" in text:
483	            final_status = "error"
484	            break
485	        if max_iterations > 1:
486	            time.sleep(poll_seconds)
487	    return _emit_json(
488	        {
489	            "ok": final_status == "complete",
490	            "kernel": kernel_ref,
491	            "status": final_status,
492	            "side_effect": SideEffect.READ_ONLY.value,
493	            "stdout": last_stdout,
494	        }
495	    )

###### 👀 Read `m9_t003_drive_reviewer_gate.py`

```
1	"""M9-T003: drive the worker to fire the reviewer-gate on kaggle_submit.
2	
3	This script:
4	  1. Creates a real agent_jobs row tied to the Spaceship Titanic baseline run.
5	  2. Runs AgentWorker with a MockLiteLLMClient that emits one synthetic
6	     `kaggle_submit` tool call (tool_decisions["kaggle_submit"]="ask"
7	     forces ApprovalRequired into _handle_approval_required).
8	  3. Forces the sync reviewer to ABSTAIN (no live LLM call) so the
9	     handler writes an agent_reviews row (verdict='abstain') AND falls
10	     through to the human-decisions branch — inserting a pending
11	     human_decisions row tied to the job.
12	  4. Prints job_id / review_id / decision_id for the closeout report.
13	
14	The script never invokes `kaggle competitions submit`. The worker stops
15	with `stop_reason="approval_required"` after pausing the job.
16	"""
17	
18	from __future__ import annotations
19	
20	import json
21	import os
22	import sys
23	import types
24	from pathlib import Path
25	
26	REPO_ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent
27	sys.path.insert(0, str(REPO_ROOT))
28	sys.path.insert(0, str(REPO_ROOT / "tools" / "kca"))
29	
30	import db as _db  # type: ignore  # noqa: E402
31	
32	from src.worker._types import JobPolicy  # noqa: E402
33	from src.worker.worker import AgentWorker, MockLiteLLMClient  # noqa: E402
34	from src.worker import reviewer as reviewer_mod  # noqa: E402
35	
36	
37	def _single_kaggle_submit_client() -> MockLiteLLMClient:
38	    """LiteLLM mock: emit one `kaggle_submit` tool call, then stop."""
39	
40	    client = MockLiteLLMClient(scenario="two_turns")
41	    turn = {"n": 0}
42	
43	    def completion(**_kwargs):
44	        turn["n"] += 1
45	        if turn["n"] == 1:
46	            tc = types.SimpleNamespace(
47	                id="call_submit_0",
48	                type="function",
49	                function=types.SimpleNamespace(
50	                    name="kaggle_submit",
51	                    arguments=json.dumps(
52	                        {
53	                            "competition": "spaceship-titanic",
54	                            "file": "runs/spaceship-titanic/baseline-lr/submission.csv",
55	                            "message": "M9-T002 baseline LR (M9-T003 reviewer gate)",
56	                        }
57	                    ),
58	                ),
59	            )
60	            msg = types.SimpleNamespace(content=None, tool_calls=[tc])
61	            choice = types.SimpleNamespace(message=msg, finish_reason="tool_calls")
62	            return types.SimpleNamespace(
63	                choices=[choice],
64	                usage=types.SimpleNamespace(prompt_tokens=20, completion_tokens=10),
65	            )
66	        msg = types.SimpleNamespace(content="done", tool_calls=None)
67	        choice = types.SimpleNamespace(message=msg, finish_reason="stop")
68	        return types.SimpleNamespace(
69	            choices=[choice],
70	            usage=types.SimpleNamespace(prompt_tokens=10, completion_tokens=5),
71	        )
72	
73	    client.completion = completion  # type: ignore[method-assign]
74	    return client
75	
76	
77	class _AbstainReviewer:
78	    """Sync reviewer stub that always abstains. Never calls a real LLM."""
79	
80	    def __init__(self, *_args, **_kwargs):
81	        self.model = "stub-abstain"
82	        self.dry_run = False
83	
84	    def review(self, _req):
85	        return reviewer_mod.ReviewVerdict(
86	            verdict="abstain",
87	            rationale="M9-T003 driver: forced abstain to exercise human-decisions path",
88	            evidence={"mode": "m9_t003_stub"},
89	            cost_usd=0.0,
90	            reviewer_model=self.model,
91	        )
92	
93	
94	def main() -> int:
95	    db_url = os.environ.get("SUPABASE_DB_URL")
96	    if not db_url:
97	        print("SUPABASE_DB_URL not set", file=sys.stderr)
98	        return 2
99	
100	    # Patch reviewer to abstain, so the handler records agent_reviews AND
101	    # falls through to insert_approval_request (human_decisions pending).
102	    reviewer_mod.Reviewer = _AbstainReviewer  # type: ignore[assignment]
103	
104	    # Build a real agent_jobs row directly (local schema lacks competition_id).
105	    policy_payload = {
106	        "max_turns": 4,
107	        "model": "claude-sonnet-4-6",
108	        "tool_decisions": {"kaggle_submit": "ask"},
109	    }
110	    import psycopg
111	    from psycopg.rows import dict_row
112	
113	    conn = psycopg.connect(db_url, row_factory=dict_row)
114	    try:
115	        with conn.cursor() as cur:
116	            cur.execute(
117	                """
118	                INSERT INTO agent_jobs
119	                  (project_id, status, prompt, model, policy, job_type)
120	                VALUES
121	                  (%s::uuid, 'queued', %s, %s, %s::jsonb, 'm9_t003_driver')
122	                RETURNING id::text
123	                """,
124	                (
125	                    _db.DEFAULT_PROJECT_ID,
126	                    "M9-T003 driver: submit spaceship-titanic baseline",
127	                    "claude-sonnet-4-6",
128	                    json.dumps(policy_payload),
129	                ),
130	            )
131	            job_id = cur.fetchone()["id"]
132	        conn.commit()
133	    finally:
134	        conn.close()
135	    print(f"job_id={job_id}")
136	
137	    policy = JobPolicy(
138	        max_turns=4,
139	        skill_name="m9-t003-driver",
140	        policy_profile="default",
141	        mode="default",
142	        tool_decisions={"kaggle_submit": "ask"},
143	    )
144	    workspace = REPO_ROOT
145	    worker = AgentWorker(
146	        job_id=job_id,
147	        prompt="M9-T003 driver: submit spaceship-titanic baseline",
148	        policy=policy,
149	        workspace=workspace,
150	        db_url=db_url,
151	        dry_run=True,  # avoid real LiteLLM in the worker main loop
152	    )
153	    worker._mock_client = _single_kaggle_submit_client()
154	    result = worker.run()
155	    print(f"worker.status={result.status} stop_reason={result.stop_reason}")
156	
157	    # Surface the agent_reviews + human_decisions rows for closeout.
158	    review = _db.find_review_for_op(job_id, "kaggle_submit")
159	    print(
160	        f"agent_reviews.id={review['id'] if review else None} verdict={review['verdict'] if review else None}"
161	    )
162	
163	    pending = _db.list_pending_decisions(job_id=job_id)
164	    print(f"human_decisions pending count={len(pending)}")
165	    if pending:
166	        print(f"human_decisions.id={pending[0]['id']} status={pending[0]['status']}")
167	
168	    # List job events so the closeout can cite the approval_pause event.
169	    events = _db.list_job_events(job_id)
170	    types_only = [
171	        (
172	            e.get("event_type"),
173	            (e.get("event_data") or {}).get("operation")
174	            or (e.get("event_data") or {}).get("target_op")
175	            or "",
176	        )
177	        for e in events
178	    ]
179	    print(f"events={types_only}")
180	
181	    return 0
182	
183	
184	if __name__ == "__main__":
185	    raise SystemExit(main())
186

    if subs:
        s = subs[0]
        score = getattr(s, 'publicScore', None) or getattr(s, 'public_score', None)
        status = getattr(s, 'status', None)
        print(f"poll t={time.time():.0f} status={status} score={score}")
        if score not in (None, '', 'null'):
            result = s
            break
        if str(status).lower() in ('error', 'failed'):
            result = s
            break
    time.sleep(5)
if result is not None:
    out = {
        "ref": str(getattr(result, 'ref', None)),
        "date": str(getattr(result, 'date', None)),
        "status": str(getattr(result, 'status', None)),
        "publicScore": str(getattr(result, 'publicScore', None) or getattr(result, 'public_score', None)),

        "fileName": str(getattr(result, 'fileName', None) or getattr(result, 'fileNameNullable', None)),
        "url": str(getattr(result, 'url', None)),
    }
    print("FINAL:", json.dumps(out, indent=2))
else:
    print("FINAL: pending (cap reached)")
EOF

1	# Milestone Loop Protocol
2	
3	_Shared rules that apply to every milestone Loop Prompt (M0+) unless a
4	milestone explicitly overrides one._
5	
6	Each `docs/m*-loop-prompts.md` should reference this file once at the top
7	rather than duplicating the rules per prompt.
8	
9	---
10	
11	## 1. Sequencing
12	
13	- Loop Prompts within a milestone MUST execute in order.
14	- Each prompt's **acceptance checks MUST pass** before moving to the next.
15	- On failure: fix the specific issue and **retry that prompt only**; do
16	  not skip ahead and do not redo prompts that already passed.
17	
18	## 2. External systems and side effects
19	
20	- Do NOT call the **real Anthropic API or Kaggle API** outside of paths
21	  the milestone explicitly designates as live; default to `--dry-run`.
22	- Do NOT run real **Kaggle submit / kernel push / dataset upload /
23	  model upload** unless the milestone explicitly requests it AND a
24	  human-approval record exists.
25	- Do NOT change **production Supabase**.
26	
27	## 3. Database validation
28	
29	- Use `SUPABASE_DB_URL=postgresql://postgres:s3cr3t@172.21.0.4:5432/postgres`
30	  — the `supabase-db` container on the local Docker network.
31	- Container IPs change on `docker compose down/up`; refresh with:
32	  ```bash
33	  docker inspect supabase-db \
34	    --format '{{range .NetworkSettings.Networks}}{{.IPAddress}}{{end}}'
35	  ```
36	- DB calls and LAN-host calls require `dangerouslyDisableSandbox=true`.
37	  Cloud LLM calls stay **inside** the sandbox.
38	
39	## 4. Reporting
40	
41	- Report **PASS / FAIL / SKIP** inline for each prompt's verification
42	  step.
43	- At milestone end, write the milestone's defined **Closeout format**
44	  (see each milestone's last Loop Prompt for the exact fields).
45	
46	## 5. Git / GitHub — worktree mode
47	
48	This project executes each milestone inside a dedicated **git worktree**
49	branched off `main`.
50	
51	- **Mid-milestone, mid-prompt:** do not `git commit` or `git push`
52	  unless the individual task spec explicitly says so. Stage with
53	  `git add` and surface diffs in the inline report.
54	- **At milestone end** — once every Loop Prompt has PASSed and the
55	  milestone's Closeout has been written — Claude Code SHOULD:
56	  1. `git add` only the files listed in the Closeout's "files changed"
57	     section (or its equivalent).
58	  2. `git commit` using either:
59	     - one squash commit per milestone, OR
60	     - one commit per Loop Prompt,
61	     depending on the milestone's preference. The default is **one
62	     commit per Loop Prompt**, with the milestone's final review as the
63	     last commit.
64	  3. `git push` the worktree's branch to the remote.
65	  4. `gh pr create` against `main` using the milestone's
66	     `docs/m{N}-final-review.md` as the PR body.
67	
68	- The following **still require explicit human approval** at any time:
69	  - `git push --force` (any branch)
70	  - `gh pr merge` (any PR)
71	  - any push to `main` directly
72	  - any `gh label create/edit/delete`, `gh issue edit/comment`,
73	    `gh pr edit/comment` against issues or PRs **not** owned by this
74	    milestone
75	
76	- If the milestone's task spec or scope says
77	  "do not commit / push / open PRs", that override **wins** — typically
78	  used for planning-only or evidence-only milestones.
79	
80	## 6. Secrets and forbidden reads
81	
82	These are always denied, regardless of milestone:
83	
84	- `.env*`
85	- `**/kaggle.json`, `~/.kaggle/kaggle.json`
86	- `~/.ssh/id_rsa`, `~/.ssh/id_ed25519`, any private key contents
87	- `~/.aws/**`, `~/.config/gcloud/**`
88	- `secrets/**`
89	
90	Shell commands that would surface the above (`cat`, `grep`, `head`,
91	`tail`, `less`, `more`, file uploads) over these paths are blocked at
92	the hook layer.
93	
94	---
95	
96	## How a milestone references this file
97	
98	In each Loop Prompt block, instead of repeating the rules above, include
99	one line near the top:
100	
101	```
102	Follow: docs/milestone-loop-protocol.md
103	```
104	
105	A milestone's `docs/m{N}-loop-prompts.md` should still spell out:
106	
107	- the milestone's own scope, non-goals, and task list;
108	- per-Loop-Prompt read lists, scope, acceptance criteria;
109	- any **override** of a default in this file (e.g. a planning-only
110	  milestone overriding the worktree commit/push behavior).
111	
````

4	M9: live end-to-end regression test — Spaceship Titanic.

8	basic feature engineering. Same CV harness as M9-T002. The deliverable is

10	real Kaggle submission** — improvement is measured by CV delta only.

41	- No kernel push, dataset / model upload.

2	
3	_Live end-to-end Kaggle regression test on
4	[Spaceship Titanic](https://www.kaggle.com/competitions/spaceship-titanic/overview)._

10	
11	## M9 at a glance
12	
13	M9 is the **first end-to-end live Kaggle regression** for this platform. It
14	exercises the M3 worker, M5 research path, M6 reviewer + telemetry, the M7
15	permission policy, and the M8 decision_api + UI shell against a real Kaggle
16	competition. The competition is Spaceship Titanic — binary classification,
17	public leaderboard, no cash prize, safe for repeated dry-run iteration and a
18	single real submission under an explicit human-approval gate.
19	
20	M9 is **not** a leaderboard-chasing milestone. The acceptance criterion is
21	that the loop *runs end-to-end correctly under the approval gates*, not that
22	the LB score is high. The CV thresholds in `docs/milestones.md` §M9 are
23	sanity guards, not targets.
24	
25	Direct entry into M9 is blocked until **all** are true:
26	
27	- M8.5-T001 (CI repair) is merged on main.

32	- `docs/m8_5-final-review.md` exists and reports PASS.
33	
34	### What's in scope
35	
36	| Capability | Owned by | M9 touches |
37	|---|---|---|
38	| Kaggle credentials handling | `env.example`, `.env`, `KAGGLE_USERNAME`/`KAGGLE_KEY` | T000 — verifies env without printing secrets; gates submit on presence |
39	| Competition register + workspace | `tools/kca/competition.py` (`register`, `clone`, `list`, `info`) | T000 / T001 |
40	| Data download + checksum | `tools/kca/kg.py::cmd_download`, `cmd_verify` (sha256 manifest already implemented in M5) | T001 |
41	| Worker loop (research → baseline → CV → submission file) | `src/worker/` + `tools/kca/run.py` + skills | T002 |
42	| Reviewer gate before submit | `src/worker/reviewer.py` + `services/decision_api/` + UI Approval Inbox | T003 |
43	| Real Kaggle submit (under approval) | `tools/kca/kg.py::cmd_submit` + `kaggle competitions submit` | T004 — single real call |
44	| Second experiment (HGB / feature engineering) | same worker, second run | T005 |

46	| GitHub issue / label workflow | `.github/labels.yml`, `.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/`, `.github/pull_request_template.md`, `policy:approval-required` | every task — work order issue per task |
47	| Final review | `milestone-final-review` skill + `worktree-milestone-pr` skill | T008 |
48	
49	### What's NOT in scope
50	
51	- Running Kaggle submit / kernel push / dataset upload / model upload outside
52	  T004's single approved call.
53	- Changing production Supabase.
54	- Implementing M9 follow-ups from M8 (multi-user auth, artifact preview via
55	  signed URLs, live-DB CI on fork PRs, OTEL collector wiring). Those are
56	  separate milestones; if M9 surfaces blockers for them, file follow-up
57	  issues — don't expand scope.
58	- Adding new CLI subcommands. M9 uses the existing `kca` surface
59	  (`competition`, `kaggle`, `run`, `research`, `review`, `decisions`,
60	  `skill`) without inventing new ones.
61	- Runtime submission-format detection. KCA's `kca kaggle submit` is
62	  format-agnostic: it passes `--file` straight to `kaggle competitions
63	  submit`, and Kaggle validates server-side. **M9 assumes
64	  `submission.csv` because Spaceship Titanic is a CSV competition.** Other
65	  competition shapes (code-competition notebooks → `kca kaggle push`;
66	  `submission.zip`; JSON; etc.) need different paths that KCA does not
67	  yet auto-select. Tracked as a separate `area:kaggle` / `type:feature`
68	  follow-up — see M9-T002's "Submission-format note" for context.

348	## Approval gates (summary)
349	
350	| Gate | When it fires | Where the approval is recorded | Who can approve |
351	|---|---|---|---|
352	| `kaggle_submit` | Worker stages a submission file and calls into `tools/kca/kg.py::cmd_submit` | `human_decisions` row + comment on the closing GitHub issue | Project owner / reviewer named on the issue |
353	| `kernel_push` | Not used in M9 | n/a (out of scope) | n/a |
354	| `dataset_upload` | Not used in M9 | n/a (out of scope) | n/a |
355	| `model_upload` | Not used in M9 | n/a (out of scope) | n/a |
356	
357	The Kaggle approval flow inside M9 is:
358	
359	```
360	worker stages submission.csv
361	  → reviewer-gate writes agent_reviews row + agent_job_events
362	  → decision_api surfaces pending decision (POST /decisions queued)
363	  → UI Approval Inbox renders pending decision
364	  → human approves via UI (POST /decisions/<id>/approve) OR
365	    `kca decisions approve --id <id>`
366	  → human comments "approved to submit" on the closing issue
367	  → triage agent promotes issue to `decision:confirmed` + `ai:ready`
368	  → M9-T004 Loop Prompt runs ONE `kca kaggle submit`
369	  → LB score recorded; submissions row written
370	  → PR opens with the approval comment linked
371	```
372	
373	A second real Kaggle submission inside M9 is **out of scope**. If a
374	follow-up experiment in M9-T005 turns out to need its own LB score,
375	file it as a new M10+ issue and gate it the same way.

396	
397	## Rollback / stop criteria
398	
399	Stop the milestone — do **not** advance to the next Loop Prompt — if any of
400	these is true:
401	
402	- A real Kaggle submit returns an error from Kaggle (rate limit, bad CSV,
403	  rules violation). The fix path is local: regenerate the submission and
404	  re-request approval; do NOT silently retry.
405	- The reviewer gate (M9-T003) fails to fire when it should, or fires
406	  when it shouldn't.
407	- Any `policy:approval-required` issue advances without the corresponding
408	  `decision:confirmed` label and comment.
409	- Any test in the validation suite regresses from green to red.
410	- The DSN, credentials, or `.env*` are accidentally printed in any log,
411	  audit row, or PR. Stop and rotate the credential immediately.
412	- CV scores diverge from the M9-T006 thresholds in a way that suggests a
413	  leakage bug (e.g. CV near 1.0). Investigate before submitting.
414	
415	If M9 needs a new architectural decision (e.g. multi-user auth, a new
416	queue, or a new artifact storage shape), **pause and ask** — those are
417	M10+ decisions, not M9 expansion. Open an ADR draft in `docs/adr/` and
418	stop the milestone there.
